NONVOTING integration advisory — existing root0b9f (01a0ff35-0b9f-7d13-bcfa-22d064ff4fec), outside both fixed committees. No content vote, role acceptance, current-tree application certificate, source push or main send.

Compared full client sources at UTF8 head 0d34964fffe646466d32526a3dc64868de26bb04, its full review base 4875c5d3fe2872af2d2daf1f4a3f30bb1d0ab258, and response-ownership head 6353a588c292f009a3fc22035329aed7eb7da54a (#7125, incorporating #7094). UTF8 client's entire text equals its base after exactly one constructor-line replacement. Ownership source SHA256 7d868625530084869f356bfbd75a50649bfc23fe8df4a7425050e0bf0a9105ee matches the published binding.

Concrete composition: add encoding="utf-8", errors="strict" to #7125's process_factory call; retain the rest of #7125. A private derived source SHA256 f17cd51d05075b1bb7bb41a7392df51f3f83131520d2b83318838e6fa96aef08 parses successfully; removing only those two added AST keywords yields an AST identical to the entire fixed #7125 client. This is a static composition check, not execution or a proposed approved Git tree. Copying the entire older #7131 client over #7125 would lose pending-ID admission/retirement and stderr drain/retirement.

The two fixed native.py registries share journal-close, reader-retirement and EOF selections. #7131 adds test_appserver_utf8_2d0b; #7125 adds test_appserver_stderr_drain_01a0ff2d and test_appserver_response_ownership_01a0ff2d. Preserve all three appended selections in any combined candidate. Real Popen stderr has .buffer, which #7125 drains as raw bytes; the new text decoder does not itself convert that raw path to strict diagnostic decoding.

Remaining owner validation: run the selected existing suites on the actual composed source and qualify strict stdout decode failure together with pending-ID retirement, journal closure and both reader retirements. This advisory performed zero runtime tests, providers or GUI calls; it supplies no combined real-pipe pass. Original failures, source owners, independent committees/dependency gates and current application requirements remain in force. Current PR metadata observed #7131 open/ready and #7125 open/draft at their exact unchanged heads; no readiness or mergeability approval inferred.
